| Key               | Default                                                                                                                                                                    | Description                                                                                             |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `include`         | `["**/*"]`                                                                                                                                                                 | Globs (relative to the workspace root) of files to index.                                               |
| `exclude`         | `.git`, `.brokspace`, `target`, `node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, lock files (`*.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `package-lock.json`, `npm-shrinkwrap.json`, `go.sum`), `*.min.js` | Globs to skip. `.gitignore` files are always honored on top of this.                                    |
| `max_file_kb`     | `512`                                                                                                                                                                      | Larger files are skipped. Binary files (NUL bytes) and non UTF-8 files are always skipped.              |
| `max_chunk_lines` | `120`                                                                                                                                                                      | A syntactic unit longer than this is split: containers into members, other nodes at line boundaries.    |
| `store`           | `auto`                                                                                                                                                                     | `auto` (LanceDB when compiled in), `lancedb` or `arrow` (memory-mapped Arrow IPC, exact vector search). |

## `embeddings` [#embeddings]

| Key          | Default                 | Description                                                                                |
| ------------ | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `enabled`    | `true`                  | `false` runs on BM25 text search only: no download, minimal memory.                        |
| `model`      | `nomic-embed-text-v1.5` | The only supported model today.                                                            |
| `variant`    | `quantized`             | `quantized` (~140 MB, int8) or `full` (~550 MB, fp32).                                     |
| `dimensions` | `768`                   | Matryoshka truncation: `64`, `128`, `256`, `512` or `768`.                                 |
| `device`     | `auto`                  | `auto`, `cpu`, `cuda`, `coreml`, `directml` (GPU devices need the matching build feature). |
| `batch_size` | `16`                    | Texts per inference batch.                                                                 |

Model files are downloaded once per user and shared by every workspace:
`~/.cache/brokspace/models` (Linux), `~/Library/Caches/brokspace/models`
(macOS), `%LOCALAPPDATA%\brokspace\models` (Windows). Set `BROK_MODELS_DIR`
to use another directory. A copy inside `.brokspace/cache/models/` (from
older versions) keeps working.

## User defaults [#user-defaults]

`brok setup llm` also stores your LLM choice in the user configuration
(`~/.config/brokspace/config.yml`, `~/Library/Application Support/brokspace/`
or `%APPDATA%\brokspace\`; override with `BROK_CONFIG_DIR`). `brok init`
applies it to every new workspace, so you choose a model once per machine.

## `search` [#search]

| Key           | Default | Description                                                                  |
| ------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `limit`       | `8`     | Default number of results.                                                   |
| `cold_weight` | `0.85`  | Score multiplier for partitions other than the one you run the command from. |

## `llm` [#llm]

OpenAI-compatible chat completion endpoints used by `brok-agent`.

```yaml
llm:
  default: ollama
  providers:
    ollama: { base_url: http://localhost:11434/v1, model: qwen2.5-coder:7b }
    lmstudio: { base_url: http://localhost:1234/v1, model: qwen2.5-coder-7b-instruct }
    anthropic:
      base_url: https://api.anthropic.com/v1
      model: claude-sonnet-5-5
      api_key_env: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
      max_tokens: 2048
```

| Key                                           | Description                                                                           |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `default`                                     | Provider used unless `brok ask --provider` says otherwise. Must exist in `providers`. |
| `providers.<name>.base_url`                   | URL up to and including `/v1`.                                                        |
| `providers.<name>.model`                      | Model name as the provider expects it.                                                |
| `providers.<name>.api_key_env`                | **Name** of the environment variable holding the key. Keys never go in this file.     |
| `providers.<name>.temperature` / `max_tokens` | Optional sampling settings.                                                           |

## `sync` [#sync]

Where the index is mirrored, configured with `brok setup sync`.

| Key                                                | Description                                                                                             |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `backend`                                          | `none`, `s3`, `r2`, `minio` or `git-lfs`.                                                               |
| `remote.bucket` / `prefix` / `region` / `endpoint` | Object storage coordinates.                                                                             |
| `remote.access_key_env` / `secret_key_env`         | Names of the variables holding the credentials (default `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`). |

`git-lfs` tracks `.brokspace/databases/**` with Git LFS and stops ignoring it,
so the index travels with the repository. The object storage sync engine
(`brok sync`) is on the roadmap: today `brok setup sync` records the target.

## `shards` [#shards]

```yaml
shards:
  brok-agent:
    enabled: true # brok run starts it (shards not listed are enabled)
    settings: # free-form, handed to the shard when it connects
      watch_interval_secs: 5
```

Each shard documents its own `settings`. For `brok-agent` see its
[README](https://github.com/brokspace/brok-agent#settings).

## Environment variables [#environment-variables]

| Variable          | Used by | Purpose                                                     |
| ----------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `RUST_LOG`        | all     | Log filter, e.g. `RUST_LOG=brok_index=debug`.               |
| `NO_COLOR`        | CLI     | Disable colors.                                             |
| `BROK_MODELS_DIR` | CLI     | Embedding model cache (default: the OS cache directory).    |
| `BROK_CONFIG_DIR` | CLI     | User defaults directory (default: the OS config directory). |
| `BROK_*` (others) | shards  | Set by `brok run` for shard processes; reserved.            |


# Getting started with Brokspace (/pt-br/docs/getting-started)

<!-- Generated from https://github.com/brokspace/brok/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md by scripts/sync-docs.mjs. Edit it there. -->

From zero to a productive workspace in about 15 minutes. Each step is short;
skip what you do not need.

1. [Install brok](#1-install-brok)
2. [Get a local LLM (optional)](#2-get-a-local-llm-optional)
3. [Set up your first workspace](#3-set-up-your-first-workspace)
4. [Use it every day](#4-use-it-every-day)
5. [Connect your coding agent](#5-connect-your-coding-agent)
6. [Configure](#6-configure)
7. [Skills](#7-skills)
8. [Shards](#8-shards)
9. [Troubleshooting](#9-troubleshooting)
10. [Update brok](#10-update-brok)
11. [Uninstall](#11-uninstall)

---

## 1. Install brok [#1-install-brok]

**macOS / Linux**

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brokspace/brok/main/scripts/install.sh | sh
```

**Windows (PowerShell)**

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brokspace/brok/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex
```

Both install two programs, `brok` and `brok-agent`, and check their
checksums. Open a new terminal and check:

```sh
brok --version
```

**Company laptop blocks the script?** Download `brok-windows-x86_64.exe`
from the [brok release](https://github.com/brokspace/brok/releases/latest)
and `brok-agent-windows-x86_64.exe` from the
[agent release](https://github.com/brokspace/brok-agent/releases/latest),
rename them `brok.exe` and `brok-agent.exe`, put both in one folder and add
that folder to your `PATH`.

**Prefer Cargo?** `cargo install brok-cli brok-agent` (needs a C compiler and
`protoc`), or `cargo install brok-cli brok-agent --no-default-features` for a
lighter build with text search only.

---

## 2. Get a local LLM (optional) [#2-get-a-local-llm-optional]

Search works without any LLM. Answers (`brok ask`, `chat`, `review`,
`commit`) need one. A local model is free, private and works offline.

**Ollama** (recommended):

| OS      | Install                                          |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| Windows | `winget install Ollama.Ollama`                   |
| macOS   | `brew install ollama`                            |
| Linux   | `curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh \| sh` |

Pick the model for your machine:

| Your machine                                                   | Model                | Download                         |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| 8 GB                                                           | `qwen2.5-coder:1.5b` | `ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:1.5b` |
| 16 GB, no GPU (most business laptops)                          | `qwen2.5-coder:3b`   | `ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:3b`   |
| 16 GB with a GPU (6 GB+) or Apple Silicon; 32 GB without a GPU | `qwen2.5-coder:7b`   | `ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:7b`   |
| A GPU with 12 GB+, or 32 GB with a GPU or Apple Silicon        | `qwen2.5-coder:14b`  | `ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:14b`  |

Not sure? Skip the pull: `brok init` (next step) measures your machine and
offers to download the right one.

Small models (1.5b, 3b) are fine for questions (`ask`, `chat`); reviews and
commit messages are much better with 7b or larger. Without a GPU, a 7b
model takes a few minutes per review, which is why the table suggests 3b
there.

Prefer a graphical app? [LM Studio](https://lmstudio.ai) works too: download a
model, open **Developer / Local Server** and press **Start Server**. More in
[Local LLM setup](/docs/local-llm).

---

## 3. Set up your first workspace [#3-set-up-your-first-workspace]

Go to your project (one repository, or a folder holding several) and run
(want a sample project first? clone
[example-nestjs](https://github.com/brokspace/example-nestjs)):

```sh
cd ~/code/my-project
brok init
```

It walks through six steps and asks before anything big:

| Step               | What happens                                                               |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1. Workspace       | Creates `.brokspace/` with a commented `brok.yml`                          |
| 2. Agent           | Installs `brok-agent`, the helper that tracks changes and talks to the LLM |
| 3. Semantic search | Downloads the search model once (~140 MB, shared by all your projects)     |
| 4. Local LLM       | Finds Ollama / LM Studio and picks a model that fits your machine          |
| 5. Index           | Indexes your code (functions, classes and sections, not raw text)          |
| 6. Coding agents   | Connects Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code or Codex (skills + search tool)      |

Want no questions? `brok init --yes` accepts every recommendation.
Then check the result:

```sh
brok doctor
```

Every line is either ✓, or a `!` with the exact command that fixes it.

> Your next project is faster: the search model and your LLM choice are
> remembered, so `brok init` there takes seconds.

---

## 4. Use it every day [#4-use-it-every-day]

```sh
brok search "where do we validate tokens"     # find code by meaning or by name
brok ask "how does the refresh flow work?"    # an answer from your LLM, with sources
brok chat                                     # a conversation with follow-up questions
brok review                                   # AI review of your uncommitted changes
git add -p && brok commit                     # commit message written from the staged diff
```

The first `ask`, `chat`, `review` or `commit` starts brok in the background.
From then on the index follows you: saved files, commits, pulls and branch
switches are picked up within seconds.

| You want to...                          | Run                                                               |
| --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Start / stop the background service     | `brok start` / `brok stop`                                        |
| Restart it after editing `brok.yml`     | `brok restart`                                                    |
| See what it is doing                    | `brok logs -f`                                                    |
| See what is indexed                     | `brok status`                                                     |
| Review only staged changes, or a branch | `brok review --staged` / `brok review --base main`                |
| Just print a commit message             | `brok commit --print`                                             |
| Use a different model for one question  | `brok ask -p anthropic "..."`                                     |
| Show whole results, or JSON for scripts | `brok search "..." --full` / `--json`                             |
| Rebuild the index from scratch          | `brok index --rebuild`                                            |
| Tab completion                          | `brok completions bash >> ~/.bashrc` (also zsh, fish, powershell) |

**About AI reviews.** With a local 7b model, `brok review` is a quick first
pass: it catches slips you would rather not push, but it also gets things
wrong (we have seen it invent a missing validation). Read its findings as
questions, not verdicts. For a review you want to rely on, use a 14b model
or a hosted one for that run: `brok review -p anthropic` (see
[Configure](#6-configure) for API keys).

Inside `brok chat`: `/skill grill-me` applies a skill to the conversation,
`/clear` forgets it, `/exit` leaves.

---

## 5. Connect your coding agent [#5-connect-your-coding-agent]

If you skipped step 6 of `brok init`:

```sh
brok setup agents
```

It detects your agents and, for each one, adds:

- a **search tool** (`brok_search`) through MCP, so the agent finds code by
  meaning before grepping;
- the **built-in skills**, such as `/ask-brok`, `/grill-me`, `/to-spec`,
  `tdd` and `code-review`.

| Agent             | Files written                                                       |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code       | `.mcp.json`, `.claude/skills/`                                      |
| Cursor            | `.cursor/mcp.json`, `.agents/skills/`                               |
| VS Code / Copilot | `.vscode/mcp.json`, `.agents/skills/`                               |
| Codex             | `.agents/skills/` (prints the MCP lines for `~/.codex/config.toml`) |

Commit these files and your whole team gets the same setup. In your agent,
start with `/ask-brok` and describe what you want to do.

---

## 6. Configure [#6-configure]

Everything lives in **`.brokspace/brok.yml`**. Every key is optional and the
defaults are sensible. The settings people change most:

```yaml
llm:
  default: ollama # which provider `brok ask` uses
  providers:
    ollama:
      base_url: http://localhost:11434/v1
      model: qwen2.5-coder:7b
    anthropic: # hosted models: the key comes from an env var
      base_url: https://api.anthropic.com/v1
      model: claude-sonnet-5-5
      api_key_env: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

embeddings:
  enabled: true # false = text search only, less memory

index:
  exclude: # .gitignore is always respected too
    - "**/node_modules/**"
    - "**/*.min.js"
    - "docs/archive/**"

shards:
  brok-agent:
    settings:
      review: # optional AI review of matching files on change
        enabled: false
        include: ["src/api/**"]
```

Easier ways to change things:

| Change                                   | Command                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Switch the local LLM or model            | `brok setup llm` (or `brok setup llm --provider ollama --model llama3:8b`) |
| Connect more coding agents               | `brok setup agents`                                                        |
| Share the index (Git LFS, S3, R2, MinIO) | `brok setup sync`                                                          |

After editing `brok.yml`, run `brok restart`. Every key is explained in
[Configuration reference](/docs/configuration).

**API keys** are never written to files: export them in your shell
(`export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...`, or `$env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = "..."` in
PowerShell) and Brokspace reads them when needed. Secrets found in your code
are removed from the context before anything is sent to an LLM.

---

## 7. Skills [#7-skills]

A skill is a small, reusable workflow for AI: a `SKILL.md` file with
instructions. Brokspace ships 20 of them.

```sh
brok skill list                                    # what is available
brok skill show tdd                                # read one
brok skill run code-review "the session handling"  # run one on your local LLM
```

**User-invoked** skills are started by you (type `/name` in your agent, e.g.
`/grill-me` before a big change). **Model-invoked** skills are picked by the
agent when the task fits (e.g. `tdd`, `code-review`).

Write your own:

```sh
brok skill new release-notes          # creates .brokspace/skills/release-notes/SKILL.md
brok skill export                     # refresh your coding agents with it
```

A workspace skill with the same name as a built-in one replaces it, so you
can tailor any built-in to your team. More in [Skills](/docs/skills).

---

## 8. Shards [#8-shards]

Shards are small programs that react to what happens in your workspace (a
file changed, a question was asked) and can publish their own events. The
agent you installed is one.

```sh
brok shard list                                             # what is installed
brok shard install https://github.com/someone/some-shard    # shows its permissions before installing
brok shard new my-shard                                     # start your own (Rust project)
brok shard new my-skills --skills-only                      # or just share skills, no code
brok restart                                                # start new shards
brok bus tail                                               # watch events live while developing
```

Every shard lists the permissions it wants in `shard.json`, and you approve
them when installing. Guide: [Shards](/docs/shards).

---

## 9. Troubleshooting [#9-troubleshooting]

Start with `brok doctor`: it checks everything and prints the fix.

| Symptom                                     | Fix                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `no answer from the agent`                  | Start your LLM (open Ollama / LM Studio), then `brok doctor`                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `ollama ... is not installed`               | `ollama pull <model>` as shown by `brok doctor`                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Answers take minutes                        | The model runs on your CPU. Normal for 7b on a laptop without a GPU (a review can take 3 to 5 minutes); for faster answers use 3b: `ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:3b`, then `brok setup llm --provider ollama --model qwen2.5-coder:3b` |
| Search misses recent code                   | `brok status`; if the daemon is stopped, `brok start` catches up                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `another brok process is writing the index` | `brok` is running in the background and already indexes for you; skip `brok index`, or `brok stop` first                                                                                                                            |
| Results come back as text only              | The search model is missing: `brok model download`                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Agent does not show the brok tools          | `brok` must be on `PATH`; run `brok setup agents` and restart the agent                                                                                                                                                             |
| Odd behavior after an upgrade               | `brok restart`; if it persists, `brok index --rebuild`                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Windows: errors about long paths            | Enable long paths (`brok doctor` shows the command) or use a shorter folder                                                                                                                                                         |

Still stuck? Run `brok logs -n 100` and ask in
[Discussions](https://github.com/brokspace/brok/discussions), including the
output of `brok doctor`.

---

## 10. Update brok [#10-update-brok]

```sh
brok upgrade --check    # is there a new version, and what changed?
brok upgrade            # shows what changed, asks, then upgrades
```

`brok upgrade` downloads the new `brok` and `brok-agent`, checks them
against the release checksums, swaps them in and restarts brok in every
workspace where it was running (each workspace's agent is refreshed on
that restart). `brok doctor` tells you when a new version is out.

Then run `brok skill export` in your workspaces so your coding agents get
the updated built-in skills.

Installed with Cargo? Upgrade with `cargo install brok-cli brok-agent`.
Coming from brok 0.2.1 or older (no `upgrade` command yet)? Run the install
command from [step 1](#1-install-brok) again, once.

---

## 11. Uninstall [#11-uninstall]

```sh
brok stop                    # in each workspace where it runs
```

Then delete:

- the `.brokspace/` folder of each workspace (plus `.agents/skills`,
  `.claude/skills` and the MCP files if you no longer want them);
- the shared model cache: `~/.cache/brokspace` (Linux),
  `~/Library/Caches/brokspace` (macOS), `%LOCALAPPDATA%\brokspace` (Windows);
- your defaults: `~/.config/brokspace` (Linux),
  `~/Library/Application Support/brokspace` (macOS), `%APPDATA%\brokspace`
  (Windows);
- the `brok` and `brok-agent` programs (`~/.local/bin`, or
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\brok` on Windows; `cargo uninstall brok-cli brok-agent`
  if you used Cargo).


# Shard Hub (prévia) (/pt-br/docs/hub)

<Callout title="Em breve">
  O Hub está sendo construído. Até ele abrir, instale shards de qualquer
  repositório git com `brok shard install <url>`.
</Callout>

O Brokspace Hub será o catálogo oficial de shards feitos pelo time do
Brokspace e, mais tarde, um registro em que qualquer pessoa poderá publicar,
no espírito do Docker Hub:

- **Shards e pacotes de skills oficiais**, revisados e versionados.
- **Instalação com um comando** pela CLI e pela Brokspace IDE.
- **Permissões às claras:** cada shard lista o que pode ler, escrever,
  executar e acessar antes de você instalá-lo.

Hoje, crie os seus com [Shards](/pt-br/docs/shards) e
[Skills](/pt-br/docs/skills), começando pelo
[template de shard](https://github.com/brokspace/brok-shard-template).


# Brokspace IDE (/pt-br/docs/ide)

A Brokspace IDE é feita sobre o [Eclipse Theia](https://theia-ide.org),
então extensões do VS Code do [Open VSX](https://open-vsx.org) funcionam
nela. Ela já vem com o `brok` e o `brok-agent` e os coloca no seu `PATH`.

![Página inicial da Brokspace IDE](/images/ide-home.png)

## Instalação [#instalação]

<Tabs items={['macOS', 'Debian / Ubuntu', 'Linux (outros)', 'Windows']}>
  <Tab value="macOS">
    ```sh
    brew install --cask brokspace/tap/brokspace-ide
    ```
    Na primeira vez, abra com clique direito > **Abrir** enquanto o app ainda
    não é notarizado.
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="Debian / Ubuntu">
    ```sh
    curl -fsSL https://brokspace.github.io/apt/brokspace-archive-keyring.gpg \
      | sudo tee /usr/share/keyrings/brokspace-archive-keyring.gpg >/dev/null
    echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/brokspace-archive-keyring.gpg] https://brokspace.github.io/apt stable main" \
      | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/brokspace.list
    sudo apt update && sudo apt install brokspace-ide
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="Linux (outros)">
    Baixe o AppImage ou o `.tar.gz` da
    [versão mais recente](https://github.com/brokspace/ide/releases/latest).
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="Windows">
    Baixe `BrokspaceIDE-<versão>-windows-x64-setup.exe` da
    [versão mais recente](https://github.com/brokspace/ide/releases/latest).
    No SmartScreen, escolha **Mais informações > Executar assim mesmo**
    enquanto o instalador ainda não é assinado.
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

A IDE se atualiza sozinha pelo GitHub Releases. Para receber respostas
escritas você precisa de um LLM: veja [LLM local](/pt-br/docs/local-llm) (a
busca funciona sem ele).

## Seus primeiros minutos [#seus-primeiros-minutos]

A janela começa enxuta: Explorer, Busca, Controle de Código-Fonte e Brokspace
à esquerda, e o **agente Brokspace** fixo à direita. Depuração, Testes e
Extensões ficam a um atalho de distância.

1. **Abra uma pasta** (Arquivo > Abrir Pasta). Se ela ainda não tem um
   workspace Brokspace, a visão Brokspace oferece **Configurar Workspace**:
   ela roda `brok init` para você.
2. **Pergunte.** Digite uma pergunta na página inicial ou no painel do
   agente: o agente Brokspace responde com o seu LLM e cita as fontes usadas;
   clique em uma fonte para abrir o arquivo naquela linha. Perguntas de
   acompanhamento mantêm a conversa. Pressione `Ctrl+Shift+A`
   (`Cmd+Shift+A` no macOS) para o **modo foco no agente**, em que o agente
   ocupa a maior parte da janela.
3. **Busque.** A visão Brokspace (o "B" dobrado na barra de atividades)
   encontra código pelo significado ou pelo nome; clique em um resultado para
   abri-lo.
4. **Revise e faça commit.** Digite `/review` no chat (ou `/review staged`,
   `/review base main`). No Controle de Código-Fonte, o botão ✨ escreve a
   mensagem de commit a partir das alterações preparadas.

## A visão Brokspace [#a-visão-brokspace]

| Seção | O que mostra |
|---|---|
| **Visão Geral** | Se o Brokspace está rodando, o modelo, o índice, a busca e Perguntar / Revisar / Commit |
| **Shards** | Cada shard instalado e seu estado; expanda um para ver o que ele lê e escreve, se usa a rede, os programas que executa, os eventos que escuta e publica, e de onde veio. Instale, crie ou remova shards pela barra de ferramentas |
| **Skills** | Fluxos de trabalho que você executa e as skills que seus agentes usam; clique para executar |

## O agente Brokspace [#o-agente-brokspace]

Toda solicitação passa pelo `brok`, que a envia ao LLM definido em
`.brokspace/brok.yml` (Ollama, LM Studio ou uma API hospedada compatível com
OpenAI). Sem um LLM, ou quando ele não responde, o agente responde com o que
o índice local encontrou, em forma de links.

| Digite | Ele executa |
|---|---|
| Uma pergunta | `brok ask` com a conversa até aqui |
| `/review` | Uma revisão das suas alterações não commitadas |
| `/review staged` | Uma revisão das alterações preparadas |
| `/review base <ref>` | Uma revisão deste branch em relação a `<ref>` |
| `/skill <nome> <entrada>` | Uma skill no seu LLM, por exemplo `/skill tdd adicionar um campo de prioridade` |

## Comandos e idiomas [#comandos-e-idiomas]

Tudo também está no menu **Brokspace** e na paleta de comandos: Configurar
Workspace, Iniciar / Parar / Reiniciar, Reconstruir Índice, Diagnóstico,
Instalar, Criar e Remover Shard, Exportar Skills para Agentes de Código,
Executar Skill, Revisar, Escrever Mensagem de Commit. A barra de status
mostra se o Brokspace está rodando e qual modelo ele usa.

A IDE está em inglês e em português do Brasil. Ela começa em português em um
sistema em português; troque em **Idioma** na página inicial.

## Como funciona [#como-funciona]

A IDE conversa com o Brokspace apenas pela CLI `brok` e sua saída JSON (veja
[Integrações](/pt-br/docs/integrations)), então ela mostra exatamente o que o
`brok` vê, e tudo o que ela faz você também pode fazer em um terminal. Ela
precisa do brok 0.2.4 ou mais recente; o que vem com ela atende.


# Introdução (/pt-br/docs)

O Brokspace (`brok`) indexa seu código (um repositório, seus submódulos ou
uma pasta inteira de repositórios) em um mecanismo de busca híbrido local,
conecta esse índice ao LLM que você escolher e o liga aos agentes de código
que você já usa. Nada sai da sua máquina, a menos que você escolha um modelo
hospedado.

## Duas formas de usar [#duas-formas-de-usar]

<Cards>
  <Card title="Modo CLI: brok" href="/pt-br/docs/getting-started">
    Em qualquer terminal e qualquer editor. `brok search`, `ask`, `chat`,
    `review`, `commit`, skills e shards. Seus agentes de código ganham a
    ferramenta `brok_search` via MCP.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Modo IDE: Brokspace IDE" href="/pt-br/docs/ide">
    O mesmo workspace em uma IDE feita em torno dele: uma página inicial que
    começa pela sua pergunta, o agente Brokspace no chat, busca, revisões e
    mensagens de commit a um clique.
  </Card>
</Cards>

Os dois compartilham a mesma pasta `.brokspace/`, então você pode alternar a
qualquer momento.

## O que você ganha [#o-que-você-ganha]

- **Busca que entende código.** Funções, classes e seções são indexadas
  inteiras e encontradas pelo significado ou pelo nome, em todos os
  repositórios.
- **Respostas com fontes.** Pergunte ao seu próprio LLM (Ollama, LM Studio ou
  um modelo hospedado) sobre o workspace; toda resposta lista o código usado.
- **Revisões e mensagens de commit** a partir das suas alterações preparadas
  ou não commitadas.
- **Skills:** 20 fluxos de trabalho para IA já incluídos (TDD, code review,
  especificações...) e os seus próprios em um `SKILL.md`.
- **Shards:** pequenos programas que reagem ao seu workspace por meio de um
  barramento de eventos local e com permissões.

## Comece [#comece]

<Cards>
  <Card title="Primeiros passos" href="/pt-br/docs/getting-started">
    Instale, configure seu primeiro workspace e use no dia a dia: cerca de 15
    minutos.
  </Card>
  <Card title="LLM local" href="/pt-br/docs/local-llm">
    Escolha um modelo adequado à sua máquina e rode com Ollama ou LM Studio.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Skills" href="/pt-br/docs/skills">
    Os fluxos de trabalho incluídos e como escrever e compartilhar os seus.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Shards" href="/pt-br/docs/shards">
    Crie integrações que reagem ao seu workspace.
  </Card>
</Cards>

O Brokspace é código aberto (MIT ou Apache-2.0). Perguntas e ideias vão para
as [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/brokspace/brok/discussions).


# Integrations (/pt-br/docs/integrations)

<!-- Generated from https://github.com/brokspace/brok/blob/main/docs/integrations.md by scripts/sync-docs.mjs. Edit it there. -->

Brokspace stays small and plugs into the tools you already use.

| Integration                                                   | How                                  | Setup               |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------- |
| Coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code / Copilot, Codex) | MCP tools + skills                   | `brok setup agents` |
| Local LLMs (Ollama, LM Studio)                                | OpenAI-compatible API                | `brok setup llm`    |
| Hosted LLMs (Anthropic, DeepSeek, any OpenAI-compatible)      | `llm.providers` in `brok.yml`        | export the API key  |
| Git and submodules                                            | change tracking, hot/cold partitions | automatic           |
| Team storage (S3, R2, MinIO, Git LFS)                         | index mirroring                      | `brok setup sync`   |
| Anything else                                                 | write a shard                        | `brok shard new`    |

## Coding agents [#coding-agents]

```sh
brok setup agents            # detects your agents and asks which to connect
brok setup agents -a claude -a cursor --yes
```

For each agent it does two things.

**1. MCP server.** Registers `brok mcp` (a stdio
[Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server) so the
agent gets two tools:

| Tool          | What it does                                                                              |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `brok_search` | Hybrid search over the local index; returns whole functions/classes with `path:start-end` |
| `brok_status` | What is indexed and whether `brok run` is active                                          |

| Agent             | File written                                  |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code       | `.mcp.json` (`mcpServers.brokspace`)          |
| Cursor            | `.cursor/mcp.json` (`mcpServers.brokspace`)   |
| VS Code / Copilot | `.vscode/mcp.json` (`servers.brokspace`)      |
| Codex             | prints the snippet for `~/.codex/config.toml` |

Existing entries in those files are preserved; only `brokspace` is added or
updated. When `brok run` is active, searches reuse its loaded model;
otherwise `brok mcp` opens the index read-only on demand.

**2. Skills.** Exports the [skills](/docs/skills) to `.claude/skills/` (Claude
Code) and `.agents/skills/` (Codex, Cursor, Copilot and others), so `/ask-brok`,
`/grill-me`, `tdd`, `code-review` and the rest are available in the agent.

Commit the generated files to give your whole team the same setup. `brok`
must be on `PATH` for agents to start `brok mcp`; `brok doctor` checks it.

## Local and hosted LLMs [#local-and-hosted-llms]

See [Local LLM setup](/docs/local-llm). Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works:

```yaml
llm:
  default: ollama
  providers:
    ollama: { base_url: http://localhost:11434/v1, model: qwen2.5-coder:7b }
    company:
      { base_url: https://llm.internal.example.com/v1, model: gpt-oss-20b, api_key_env: COMPANY_LLM_KEY }
```

## Editors and scripts: JSON output [#editors-and-scripts-json-output]

Editors (the Brokspace IDE among them), scripts and CI read brok through
`--json`. Shapes are stable within a minor version.

| Command                                                                  | Output                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `brok status --json`                                                     | One document: `version`, `initialized`, `root`, `daemon.running`, `backends`, `embeddings`, `llm` (`provider`, `model`, `base_url`), `index[]` (`tier`, `path`, `files`, `chunks`, `backend`, `semantic`), `shards[]` (`name`, `version`, `description`, `state`, `source`). Outside a workspace: `{"version": ..., "initialized": false}`. |
| `brok search <query> --json`                                             | One document: `hits[]` with `path`, `start_line`, `end_line`, `kind`, `symbol`, `score`, `content`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `brok skill list --json`                                                 | One array: `name`, `description`, `user_invoked`, `source`, `bucket` per skill.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `brok ask ... --json`, `brok review --json`, `brok skill run ... --json` | A stream, one JSON event per line (see below).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

Streaming events:

```json
{"type": "chunk", "text": "Refresh tokens rotate on every "}
{"type": "chunk", "text": "use..."}
{"type": "done", "provider": "ollama", "model": "qwen2.5-coder:7b",
 "sources": [{"path": "src/auth/auth.service.ts", "start_line": 42, "end_line": 77, "symbol": "refresh"}]}
```

A failure ends the stream with a non-zero exit code and the message on
stderr. Follow-up questions pass the conversation so far:
`brok ask --json --history turns.json "and where is it tested?"`, where
`turns.json` holds `[{"role": "user", "content": "..."}, {"role":
"assistant", "content": "..."}]`.

## Shards: integrations you build [#shards-integrations-you-build]

When something is specific to your team (a ticketing system, a deploy
pipeline, a compliance check), write a shard instead of waiting for a core
feature: it reacts to workspace events and publishes its own. See
[Shards](/docs/shards) and start with `brok shard new my-integration`.


# Local LLM setup (/pt-br/docs/local-llm)

<!-- Generated from https://github.com/brokspace/brok/blob/main/docs/local-llm.md by scripts/sync-docs.mjs. Edit it there. -->

Brokspace answers questions (`brok ask`) and runs skills (`brok skill run`)
with any OpenAI-compatible model. Running it locally keeps everything
**free, private and offline**. Search and indexing never need an LLM.

## The short version [#the-short-version]

```sh
brok setup llm      # also part of `brok init`
```

It:

1. reads your RAM (and NVIDIA GPU memory) and picks a model size from the
   table below;
2. looks for a running **Ollama** (`localhost:11434`) or **LM Studio**
   (`localhost:1234`) server;
3. uses a model you already have, or offers to download the recommended one
   (`ollama pull`);
4. writes the choice to `.brokspace/brok.yml` (`llm.default`).

Nothing installed yet? It prints the one-line install for your OS. Run it,
then `brok setup llm` again. `brok doctor` tells you at any time whether the
model is reachable.

## What your machine can run [#what-your-machine-can-run]

Sizes are for 4-bit quantized models (`Q4_K_M`), the best balance between
speed and quality.

| Model size                | Memory and GPU                                                 | Typical hardware                          | Recommended (Ollama)                              |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| 1B to 3B                  | 8 GB                                                           | Office laptops, entry-level Macs          | `qwen2.5-coder:1.5b`, `llama3.2:3b`               |
| 3B                        | 16 GB, no GPU                                                  | Business laptops with integrated graphics | `qwen2.5-coder:3b`, `llama3.2:3b`                 |
| **7B to 9B** (sweet spot) | 16 GB with a GPU (6 GB+) or Apple Silicon; 32 GB without a GPU | Gaming laptops, M1/M2/M3 Macs, desktops   | `qwen2.5-coder:7b`, `llama3:8b`, `deepseek-r1:8b` |
| 14B to 32B                | A GPU with 12 GB+, or 32 GB with a GPU or Apple Silicon        | Workstations, Mac Pro/Max with 32 GB+     | `qwen2.5-coder:14b`, `deepseek-r1:32b`            |

Without a GPU the model runs on the processor: memory decides what fits,
but speed decides what is pleasant. A laptop CPU reads a long prompt into a
7B model at about 15 tokens per second, so a review takes 3 to 5 minutes;
a 3B model is about twice as fast. That is why machines without a GPU get
one size smaller. Only NVIDIA GPUs and Apple Silicon are detected; with
another GPU that Ollama supports, pick the row for your GPU memory.

What to expect: 1B to 3B models answer questions about your code well
enough (`brok ask`, `brok chat`), but they lose track of longer skills, so
`brok review`, `brok commit` and most `brok skill run` workflows are much
better with 7B or larger. Even at 7B, a review is a first pass that can be
wrong; 14B and hosted models (`brok review -p anthropic`) review much
better, and commit messages are already good at 7B.

`brok setup llm` applies exactly this table. Override it any time:

```sh
brok setup llm --provider ollama --model llama3:8b
```

## Option 1: Ollama (recommended, terminal friendly) [#option-1-ollama-recommended-terminal-friendly]

| OS      | Install                                                                               |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows | `winget install Ollama.Ollama` or the installer from [ollama.com](https://ollama.com) |
| macOS   | `brew install ollama` or the app from [ollama.com](https://ollama.com)                |
| Linux   | `curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh \| sh`                                      |

```sh
ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:7b     # or let `brok setup llm` do it
brok setup llm
```

## Option 2: LM Studio (graphical) [#option-2-lm-studio-graphical]

1. Download it from [lmstudio.ai](https://lmstudio.ai) (Windows `.exe`,
   macOS `.dmg` for Apple Silicon or Intel, Linux `.AppImage`:
   `chmod +x LM_Studio-*.AppImage && ./LM_Studio-*.AppImage`).
2. Search for `Qwen2.5-Coder-7B` (or the size from the table), pick a
   `Q4_K_M` or `Q5_K_M` file and download it.
3. Open the **Developer / Local Server** tab, load the model and press
   **Start Server** (it listens on `http://localhost:1234`).
4. Run `brok setup llm`: it finds the server and lets you pick the model.

## Hosted models [#hosted-models]

Prefer a hosted model for some questions? Export its key and choose it per
request; the providers are preconfigured in `brok.yml`:

```sh
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...        # PowerShell: $env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = "..."
brok ask -p anthropic "explain the retry policy"
```

Keys are read from the environment, never stored in `brok.yml`, and secrets
found in retrieved code are redacted before any prompt leaves your machine.

## Using the same model elsewhere [#using-the-same-model-elsewhere]

- **Aider**: `aider --model ollama/qwen2.5-coder:7b` inside your git
  repository (`pip install aider-chat`, Python 3.10 to 3.12).
- **Coding agents** (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Codex): `brok setup agents`
  gives them the Brokspace search tool and skills; see
  [Integrations](/docs/integrations).

## Performance tips [#performance-tips]

- **Apple Silicon**: memory is unified, so a 16 GB Mac runs 7B/8B models fast.
- **NVIDIA / AMD GPUs**: enable full GPU offload in LM Studio or Ollama.
- **Storage**: keep models on an SSD; loading from a spinning disk is painfully slow.
- **Smaller is often better** for interactive use: a fast 7B beats a slow
  14B for everyday questions; switch per request with `-p`.


# Shards (/pt-br/docs/shards)

<!-- Generated from https://github.com/brokspace/brok/blob/main/docs/shards.md by scripts/sync-docs.mjs. Edit it there. -->

Shards are small programs that react to workspace events. Each one is a
separate process connected to the `brok run` event bus, restricted to the
topics its manifest declares.

The fastest way to write one is the
[brok-shard-template](https://github.com/brokspace/brok-shard-template)
repository; this page is the reference.

## Lifecycle [#lifecycle]

```sh
brok shard new my-shard                  # project from brok-shard-template
brok shard new my-skills --skills-only   # a skill shard: shard.json + skills/
brok shard install ./my-shard            # local directory (development)
brok shard install https://github.com/acme/brok-license-check --tag v1.0.0
brok start                               # starts every enabled shard (or `brok restart`)
brok bus tail 'license:*'                # watch what it publishes
brok shard remove brok-license-check
```

To trigger your shard by hand, publish the event it listens to:
`brok bus emit file:changed '{"changed":["src/main.rs"],"deleted":[]}'`.
Windows PowerShell 5.1 drops the inner double quotes when it calls a
program, so escape them there: `'{\"changed\":[\"src/main.rs\"],\"deleted\":[]}'`
(PowerShell 7 and other shells need no escaping).

Installing:

1. clones the repository (`--depth 1`, optional `--tag`) or uses the local directory;
2. validates `shard.json` and the `brok` version requirement;
3. **shows the requested capabilities and asks for consent** (`--yes` to skip in scripts);
4. obtains the executable, in order of preference:
   - a release asset for this platform, verified against its SHA-256;
   - the manifest's `build.command`, run in the repository;
   - an `entrypoint` already present in the repository;
5. moves it into `.brokspace/shards/<name>/` and records the source, commit and
   binary hash in `shards.lock`.

Disable a shard without removing it in `brok.yml`:

```yaml
shards:
  brok-license-check:
    enabled: false
```

## `shard.json` [#shardjson]

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brokspace/brok-sdk/main/shard.schema.json",
  "name": "brok-security-auditor",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "Flags risky changes in source files",
  "license": "MIT",
  "repository": "https://github.com/acme/brok-security-auditor",
  "brok": ">=0.1.0, <0.2.0",
  "entrypoint": "bin/security-auditor",
  "args": [],
  "runtime": "native",
  "permissions": {
    "filesystem": { "read": ["src/"], "write": [] },
    "network": false,
    "process": ["git"],
    "env": ["SEMGREP_*"]
  },
  "subscribes_to": ["file:changed"],
  "publishes_to": ["security:alert"],
  "build": { "command": ["cargo", "build", "--release"], "artifact": "target/release/security-auditor" },
  "releases": {
    "linux-x86_64": { "url": "https://github.com/acme/…/security-auditor-linux-x86_64", "sha256": "…" },
    "macos-aarch64": { "url": "https://github.com/acme/…/security-auditor-macos-aarch64", "sha256": "…" },
    "windows-x86_64": {
      "url": "https://github.com/acme/…/security-auditor-windows-x86_64.exe",
      "sha256": "…"
    }
  }
}
```

| Field                               | Required | Rules                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`                              | ✓        | `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,63}$`, unique in the workspace                                                                                  |
| `version`                           | ✓        | SemVer                                                                                                                             |
| `entrypoint`                        | ✓¹       | Relative path inside the shard directory; `.exe` is appended on Windows                                                            |
| `skills`                            | ✓¹       | Directories whose subfolders each hold a `SKILL.md` ([skills](/docs/skills))                                                       |
| `brok`                              |          | SemVer requirement on the runtime version                                                                                          |
| `runtime`                           |          | `native` (default)                                                                                                                 |
| `permissions.filesystem.read/write` |          | Workspace relative paths, no `..`, no absolute paths                                                                               |
| `permissions.network`               |          | `false` by default                                                                                                                 |
| `permissions.process`               |          | Bare program names the shard intends to run                                                                                        |
| `permissions.env`                   |          | Variables to pass through: exact names, `PREFIX_*` or `*_SUFFIX`. `BROK_*` is reserved                                             |
| `subscribes_to` / `publishes_to`    |          | Topic patterns; publishing to `system:*` (or `*`) is not allowed                                                                   |
| `build.command`                     |          | Program + arguments, executed **without a shell**                                                                                  |
| `releases.<os>-<arch>`              |          | `https://` URL and 64 hex SHA-256; keys use Rust's `std::env::consts` names (`linux-x86_64`, `macos-aarch64`, `windows-x86_64`, …) |

¹ A shard needs an `entrypoint`, `skills`, or both. Skill-only shards run no
process, so they cannot declare topics, `build` or `releases`.

Unknown fields are rejected, and all violations are reported at once.

## Topics [#topics]

`namespace:name`, lowercase letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.` for sub-topics:
`file:changed`, `agent:ask.chunk`. Patterns are exact topics or a prefix
ending in `*` (`agent:ask.*`, `file:*`, `*`). Pick a namespace named after
your shard for your own events. The well-known topics and their payloads are
listed in [Architecture](/docs/architecture#well-known-topics).

## Runtime contract [#runtime-contract]

`brok run` starts the entrypoint with:

- working directory = workspace root;
- an environment containing only OS basics (`PATH`, `HOME`, `TEMP`, …),
  `RUST_LOG`, the variables allowed by `permissions.env`, and:

| Variable                         | Value                              |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `BROK_ENDPOINT`                  | Socket path / pipe name of the bus |
| `BROK_TOKEN`                     | The shard's session token (secret) |
| `BROK_SHARD_NAME`                | Manifest name                      |
| `BROK_WORKSPACE`                 | Absolute workspace root            |
| `BROK_FS_READ` / `BROK_FS_WRITE` | Declared paths, `;`-separated      |
| `BROK_NETWORK`                   | `1` or `0`                         |

- stdout and stderr are captured line by line, prefixed with the shard name in
  the `brok run` output and appended to `.brokspace/logs/<name>.log`. Log to
  stderr.
- On `system:shutdown` (delivered without subscribing), exit within 3 seconds.
- A non-zero exit is a crash: the shard is restarted with backoff.

## Using the SDK [#using-the-sdk]

```rust
use brok_sdk::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), ClientError> {
    let (client, mut inbox) = BrokClient::connect_from_env("my-shard", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")).await?;
    client.subscribe([TopicPattern::new("file:changed")?]).await?;

    while let Some(event) = inbox.recv().await {
        if event.is::<Shutdown>() {
            break;
        }
        if let Ok(change) = event.decode::<FileChanged>() {
            for path in change.changed {
                // … inspect the file, then publish your own event:
                // client.emit(&MyFinding { path, … }).await?;
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

- Typed payloads implement `brok_sdk::Payload` (a serde type plus its topic).
- `client.request(event)` returns a stream of replies; `client.call::<Req,
  Res>(&req, timeout)` waits for the first typed reply. Example: query the
  index with `client.call::<SearchRequest, SearchResults>(…)` (add
  `index:search` to `publishes_to`).
- `client.reply(&request, &payload)` answers a request; only the requester
  receives it.
- `client.context()` returns the workspace root, your `shards.<name>.settings`
  from `brok.yml` and the `llm` routing table.

Shards do not have to be written in Rust: anything that can open a Unix
socket / named pipe and exchange length-prefixed JSON frames works. The frame
format is documented in `brok-sdk/src/frame.rs` and `codec.rs`.

## Security [#security]

What the runtime **enforces**: topic ACLs, `source` stamping, reply routing,
the scrubbed environment, the working directory.

What is **declared but not yet enforced by the OS**: file system and network
access. Consent at install time is the safeguard until OS sandboxes (Landlock,
Seatbelt, AppContainer) land. `build.command` runs arbitrary code from the
shard repository (e.g. `build.rs`) — the consent prompt shows it before it
runs. Prefer shards that publish checksum-pinned `releases`.


# Skills (/pt-br/docs/skills)

<!-- Generated from https://github.com/brokspace/brok/blob/main/docs/skills.md by scripts/sync-docs.mjs. Edit it there. -->

A **skill** is a small, reusable workflow written for AI agents: a folder
with a `SKILL.md` (YAML frontmatter `name` + `description`, then
instructions) and optional reference files. Brokspace uses the same
[Agent Skills](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills) format as Claude Code,
Codex, Cursor and GitHub Copilot, so a skill written once works everywhere.

```text
code-review/
├── SKILL.md            name, description, instructions
├── agents/openai.yaml  display metadata for Codex (optional)
└── CHECKLIST.md        reference material linked from SKILL.md (optional)
```

## Two kinds [#two-kinds]

|               | User-invoked                                | Model-invoked                                |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Who starts it | Only you, by typing `/name`                 | You, or the agent when the task fits         |
| Frontmatter   | `disable-model-invocation: true`            | (default)                                    |
| Role          | Orchestrates a flow (`/to-spec`, `/triage`) | A reusable discipline (`tdd`, `code-review`) |
| Description   | One human-facing line                       | Rich "Use when..." triggers                  |

## Built-in skills [#built-in-skills]

`brok` ships a curated set, embedded in the binary (source:
[skills/](https://github.com/brokspace/brok/blob/main/skills/README.md)). They cover the whole development loop that
Brokspace itself uses: align, specify, slice, build test-first, review, ship.

```sh
brok skill list          # everything available, with its source
brok skill show tdd      # read one
```

Not sure where to start? Type `/ask-brok` in your coding agent and describe
your situation.

## Using skills [#using-skills]

**In your coding agent** (the main way):

```sh
brok setup agents        # skills + MCP search tool, for the agents it detects
brok skill export        # skills only; --agent claude|agents|cursor|vscode|codex, --global
```

Skills land in `.claude/skills/` and the portable `.agents/skills/` (read by
Codex, Cursor, Copilot and others). Folders are marked `.brokspace-managed`
and refreshed on every export; brok never overwrites a folder it did not
create. Commit them to share with your team.

**On your local LLM**, through `brok-agent` (needs `brok run`):

```sh
brok skill run code-review "the changes in src/api since main"
brok skill run grill-me "plan: move sessions to redis"
```

The skill's instructions (and the reference files it links) become the
system prompt; Brokspace adds relevant code from the index as context.

## Writing your own [#writing-your-own]

```sh
brok skill new release-notes                  # model-invoked, in .brokspace/skills/
brok skill new deploy --user-invoked          # a /deploy workflow only you trigger
```

Workspace skills in `.brokspace/skills/<name>/` **override** built-ins with
the same name, so you can tailor any built-in to your team. Keep skills
short and explicit: small local models follow them too. The built-in
`write-skill` skill walks your agent through it.

## Sharing skills: skill shards [#sharing-skills-skill-shards]

A **skill shard** is a shard with no process, just skills. Publish it as a
git repository and anyone can install it:

```sh
brok shard new acme-skills --skills-only      # shard.json + skills/example/
# edit, push to GitHub, then on any machine:
brok shard install https://github.com/acme/acme-skills
brok skill list                               # source: shard:acme-skills
```

`shard.json` of a skill shard:

```json
{ "name": "acme-skills", "version": "0.1.0", "skills": ["skills"] }
```

A shard can also ship skills next to its process (`entrypoint` + `skills`).

## Precedence [#precedence]

When names collide, the first wins: workspace (`.brokspace/skills/`) >
installed shards > built-in. `brok skill list` reports shadowed skills.

## Credits [#credits]

The built-in workflows are adapted from
[mattpocock/skills](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills) (MIT); see
[skills/CREDITS.md](https://github.com/brokspace/brok/blob/main/skills/CREDITS.md).
